 When Democrats take over Congress in January, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. will be a major oversight target. His changes to vaccine guidance and cuts to medical research have sparked criticism. Some lawmakers have suggested impeachment, and probes into his actions are underway. However, Democrats also want to find common ground with Kennedy’s Make America Healthy Again supporters. This balance is tricky since many MAHA activists still see Kennedy as an ally. Democrats will try to hold him accountable while collaborating on shared interests like regulating pesticides and improving school lunches. They'll also have to work to lower health costs.

 NEW YORK (AP) — When Democrats take over Congress in January, one of their many oversight targets will be Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., whose overhaul of longstanding vaccine guidance and cuts to medical research over the past two years have drawn fiery criticism. Some high-ranking lawmakers have suggested impeaching him.
 But those efforts could conflict with another growing priority for many lawmakers on the left: nurturing areas of common ground with Kennedy’s Make America Healthy Again followers with the aim of securing their political support.
